judgment.notes: N001 is instantiated with m=1, A=I and positive exponents a>1 or 0<s<1. Its zero/infinite-measure implications give precisely the respective dimension bounds. The routine measure, endpoint, series and power facts have their required conditions, as detailed in BG001–BG005; no measurability of the covering sets is used.

The N equal subintervals give arbitrarily small cost at each fixed positive scale for a>1. Enlarging each bounded nonempty covering set yields open intervals with total added length at most epsilon, so every cover has total diameter at least 1, including the infinite-sum case. For 0<s<1 the positive finite factor delta^(s-1) gives a uniform lower bound on every cover cost. Infimum over covers and supremum over scales therefore give infinite measure. The two families of dimension bounds imply dimension exactly 1.

scope: Coverage is reviewer-reported; reading alone is not mathematical assessment.
